notes:
Initial outreach 2025-08: product fit for low-latency personalization/chat. SE-led demo 2025-10 showed Redwood batching and cost controls — impressed with latency numbers. POC started Nov 2025 (analytics + personalization bundle)

Sales notes (shorthand):
- CTO = Elena Park (heavy GCP primacy)
- Infra team: full GCP, strong preference for Vertex endpoints due to existing GCP IAM + VPC-native routing
- Security: requested SOC2 + KMS + detailed audit logging examples; had an internal checklist that favored managed cloud endpoints (reduced attack surface)
- Budget: mid-Q4 freeze, then restarted Jan 2026 with procurement push for vendor consolidation

POC feedback:
- Performance: Redwood POC matched latency targets (p95 ~110ms) on our test traffic
- Cost: Redwood unit cost looked competitive in isolation; finance worried about multi-vendor invoicing and discounting complexity
- Ops: devops commented: "we want 0 ops — prefer vendor-managed endpoints inside GCP so infra team doesn't add another stack"

Final negotiations:
- Starglow asked for deeper committed discount + integration assistance (single-sign on, drive connectors). Redwood proposal included Private offering + migration credits.
- Security team remained concerned about cross-cloud key management; GCP KMS + Vertex offered simpler compliance mapping for them

Outcome summary:
- Procurement selected GCP Vertex AI native endpoints (decision 2026-02). Primary reasons: single-vendor standardization, committed cloud discount, lower perceived ops burden. Security exec: "company policy is to standardize on hyperscaler managed endpoints where possible."

Sales coach notes:
- No clear internal champion after the CTO handed procurement to vendor-management team in Jan 2026. Champion drifted to infra lead who prioritized platform consistency.
- Lessons: emphasize multi-cloud integration story earlier; quantify cross-vendor ops cost; propose a migration path that includes managed connector for cloud native stacks.

use_case_summary: Starglow runs real-time personalization and conversational hooks inside their ad targeting stack. Needs: p95 latency <150ms, per-request embedding lookups, and embedding storage + semantic search. High throughput during campaigns; cost sensitivity around peak season. Wanted private/VPC deployment for IP protection.
decision_summary: Closed-lost: Starglow selected GCP Vertex AI native endpoints. Key drivers: existing GCP-only infra, procurement mandate to consolidate vendors, committed cloud discount from Google, and security preference for hyperscaler-managed endpoints which fit their compliance map. No single internal champion emerged after CTO delegated to platform team; budget negotiations squeezed Redwood's margin on proposed committed spend levels.
